blocks.h2: Disposals in Buildings With Shared Drains
blocks.body: In a condo or two-flat, a disposal sends ground food into a drain that other units also use. Ground food mixed with grease can settle in an old horizontal line and cause clogs that affect more than one unit. Running plenty of cold water, keeping grease out and not overloading the disposal helps the whole building. If the shared line clogs often, a camera look can show where the buildup is.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of a Disposal Job
blocks.body: A straight swap is quick. A first-time install in an older kitchen may need an outlet and drain changes. A slow shared drain should be cleared first. We check and quote one flat price.

blocks.h2: Garbage Disposal Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: Can you install a disposal in an older kitchen?
items.answer: Usually. We may need to add an outlet and adjust the drain.

items.q: My disposal hums. What should I do?
items.preview: Turn it off. It's likely jammed.
items.answer: Turn it off. Try the reset button and the hex key under the unit. If it won't turn, call us.

items.q: Can a disposal clog an old drain?
items.answer: It can, especially with grease, fibrous food and coffee grounds.

items.q: Should I repair or replace it?
items.preview: If it leaks from the body or is old, replace it.
items.answer: If the housing leaks or it's more than about 10 years old, replacing it usually makes more sense.

items.q: Is my condo allowed to have a disposal?
items.answer: Check with your association. Most allow them.

items.q: My disposal won't start. What should I check?
items.preview: The reset button and the switch.
items.answer: Press the red reset button under the unit and check the wall switch and breaker. If it still won't start, call us.

items.q: How much does garbage disposal installation cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on the unit. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the unit and connections. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
